memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "and after a while his master's wife took notice of Joseph and said, 'Come to bed with me!'" - Gen 39:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Just when things are going well for Joseph, temptation arrives. His master's wife takes notice of him and issues a bold, direct invitation to sin: "Come to bed with me!" Notice the timing. Joseph was being faithful, prospering in his work, carrying God's blessing — and it is precisely then that a powerful temptation strikes.

This is often how temptation works. It does not always come when we are weak and struggling; sometimes it comes when things are going well, when we feel secure and successful. Seasons of blessing can be seasons of special danger, because we may let down our guard, thinking we are strong. The enemy of our souls is happy to strike at our high points.

Notice also who is doing the tempting: not a stranger, but the wife of his master, a person of power and influence, someone Joseph could not easily avoid. Temptation often comes through the people and situations closest to us, and sometimes through those who hold power over us.

None of us is beyond temptation. Even a young man walking faithfully with God faced this. So we should never grow complacent or assume we are immune. "If you think you are standing firm, be careful that you don't fall" (1 Cor 10:12). Stay watchful, especially in your good seasons, and be ready — as Joseph was — to say no.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Are you most tempted to let down your guard when things are going well?
Do you stay watchful, or assume you are immune to temptation?
How can you prepare now to say no before temptation comes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me watchful against temptation, especially in my good seasons. Do not let me grow complacent or overconfident. Prepare my heart now to stand firm and say no. Amen.
